Package hadur.bench

Class ShieldProbe

java.lang.Object
hadur.bench.ShieldProbe
final class ShieldProbe extends Object
BENCH-11: the shield probe. --shield-probe FILE names a set of opponents (the usual set format, name | role | jar | weight) to run with Hadur's shield mode on and off over the same seeds, and report the paired difference for each.

Shield mode is switched by the list in the robot jar, the class hadur2.ShieldListData (SHIELD-5; a class because Robocode's sandbox denies a robot the read of a resource in its own jar). The probe repacks the candidate jar twice: once with that class naming every opponent of the set ("on") and once with a list of comments only ("off"); it writes the class's source and compiles it with the JDK's compiler. The two get distinct robot versions (<version>-on, <version>-off) in their Hadur.properties, so Robocode installs them side by side, and then the existing paired machinery runs them: the "on" jar as the candidate, the "off" jar as the baseline (--baseline, BENCH-2), one battle each per seed at the same RANDOMSEED. The two jars are otherwise the same bytes, so the difference is shield mode and nothing else.

prepare(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>, java.nio.file.Path) rewrites the options and makes the jars; render(java.util.Map<hadur.bench.Opponent, java.util.List<hadur.bench.BattleResult>>, java.util.Map<hadur.bench.Opponent, java.util.List<hadur.bench.BattleResult>>, java.nio.file.Path, java.lang.String, java.lang.String) writes the report section: per opponent the paired difference with its interval, a verdict, what shield mode did in the "on" battles (read from the SH and SR records in their hadur.log), the panel's weighted mean difference, and the opponents that beat the list's bar, ready to paste into the shield list.

    • prepare

      static void prepare(Map<String,String> opts, Path benchDir) throws IOException
      Turns --shield-probe FILE into a paired run: the set is the probe's file, the candidate is the "on" jar and the baseline is the "off" jar. Does nothing when the option is absent. Must run before the options are read.
      Parameters:
      opts - the options; robot, robot-jar, set, baseline, baseline-robot and out are filled in
      benchDir - the bench's working directory, where relative paths start
      Throws:
      IOException - if the jar cannot be read or the new ones written

    • repack

      static void repack(Path source, Path target, String version, String list) throws IOException
      Copies source to target with its shield list replaced and its robot version set. Every other entry is copied unchanged.
      Parameters:
      source - the candidate jar
      target - the jar to write
      version - the robot version string to put in PROPERTIES_ENTRY
      list - the list's text, one entry per line, compiled into LIST_ENTRY
      Throws:
      IOException - if reading or writing fails
      IllegalStateException - if the source has no shield list class or no properties entry, so it predates shield mode (a repack would then change nothing)
